claims.claim: Continuous post-deployment monitoring can detect meaningful divergence earlier than one-time approval systems when relevant signals are observable.
falsification_examples: A one-time approval baseline detects divergence at the same or earlier time across controlled simulations.
Monitoring signals systematically fail to correlate with meaningful divergence.

claims.claim: Stakeholder signals can expose harms not visible in executive business KPIs alone.
falsification_examples: Stakeholder sensing adds no new predictive information in empirical cases.
Stakeholder signals produce materially worse governance outcomes because of noise or manipulation.

claims.claim: Adaptive restriction of authority can reduce repeated harm after poor outcomes, subject to false-positive controls.
falsification_examples: Static authority performs as well or better under repeated comparable failures.
Adaptive authority creates more systemic harm through instability or gaming.

claims.claim: Signed human authorization of consequential agent recommendations improves accountability traceability.
falsification_examples: Signature records do not improve post-hoc attribution or review quality.
Signatures systematically become ceremonial rubber stamps.

expected_behaviors: Poor stakeholder signals can RESTRICT a decision despite good outcome scores.

review_questions: Are the state transitions internally consistent?
Are threshold values arbitrary or empirically justified?
Can the model distinguish decision quality from implementation quality?
Does reputation-linked authority create perverse incentives?
Which claims are conceptual versus empirically supported?
